Council portrait base — draft for review

Rough procedural base, not finished art. It exists to fix the framing, proportions and state list before anyone paints over it.

The five states

Talk loop — two frames, alternating

This is why the state list needs pairs. Speech is a two-frame alternation between mouth-closed and mouth-open in the same mood. Left is neutral, right is angry.

Framing — at true rendered tile size

Bottom row is the face region at real pixels, magnified with no smoothing, so the legibility question is answered honestly rather than by eye at 4x.

Proportion guide

Landmarks an artist aligns to. Blue lines are head units (6 heads to the figure, not a realistic 7.5 — see note). Orange lines are anatomical landmarks. White verticals are the safe margin.

Why 6 heads and not 7.5: a realistic figure at this tile size puts the head at about 40px, and an angry brow at 40px is invisible. Six heads keeps the face readable while still reading as an adult rather than a chibi. This is the single most important constraint on the base — if your art uses realistic proportions, the expressions stop working.
